summary: The 5-acre waterfront park delivered with Mission Rock's Phase 1; SF YIMBY reports that SCAPE Studio was responsible for its master design and that Webcor was the general contractor. An opening celebration was held on the morning before SF YIMBY's April 26, 2024 article. The Port says the City has accepted all Phase 1 public infrastructure, including parks.

milestones.text: Opening celebration held for China Basin Park (SF YIMBY's April 26, 2024 article says it was held 'yesterday morning', so April 25)

Port Commission passes Resolutions 25-05 and 25-06 unanimously to accept Phase 1 public infrastructure; staff say 'First is China Basin Park and Port open spaces' and that the park will be 'completely Port owned'
Port staff report says the Developer completed Phase 1 in 2025 and 'the City has accepted all public infrastructure, including parks, streets, and public utilities within the Phase'

facts.value: 5 acres (Port staff report, June 2026). Pier & Point's mapped lot 8719A005 is about 4.69 ac less the Block K lobe, so the figures are not directly comparable.
SCAPE Studio is 'responsible for the master design of the China Basin Park' (SF YIMBY)
Webcor ('Webcor was the general contractor', SF YIMBY)
'The Bay Trail, which runs through the park' (SF YIMBY)

sources.title: Mission Rock opens waterfront park, starts leasing for Verde (SF YIMBY, April 26, 2024)
Minutes of the Port Commission meeting, February 11, 2025 (Mission Rock Phase 1 acceptance; Resolutions 25-05 and 25-06)

Informational presentation on updates to the Mission Rock Development Project, including efforts to accelerate Phase 2, with possible action on a Port Capital investment of $10 million (Port Commission Item 11A, Resolution 26-34)

open_questions: Park cost is not published separately in any source read.
The Port's 5-acre figure and the mapped lot area differ; which boundary the Port counts is not stated.
